behaviors.behavior: AC1: a duplicate sentence embedded in a longer narrative is stripped, but the rest of the narrative and any genuinely different narrative stays visible
behaviors.evidence: missionActivityFeedText.test.ts (stripDuplicateSentence unit cases) + MissionActivityFeed.test.tsx (PR-dedup regression + 'keeps a genuinely different narrative sentence visible' test)

behaviors.behavior: AC2: a user-typed ('You') card renders with a greenish-tinted background and light-fill user icon, distinct from every other card
behaviors.reason: A pure CSS color/tint decision (mission-operation.css [data-kind="user"] rules) with no seedable behavioral precondition to drive from a real transcript — same established convention this file's own history already applies to the Delivered-box CSS spacing fix (verified by direct inspection + existing CSS cascade). The card's existence/content at data-kind="user" is already covered structurally by mission-feed-transcript-fidelity.spec.ts.

behaviors.behavior: AC3: a delegated Agent/Task dispatch renders a running subrunner card, then resolves via task-notification to a report openable in a right-side panel
behaviors.evidence: missionActivityFeedSubrunner.test.ts (24+ unit cases incl. Agent/Task dispatch, ack correlation, unknown-status no-op, same-id collision) + SubrunnerPanel.test.tsx + mission-subrunner.spec.ts (Playwright, real Chromium via isolated-stack.mjs; F0.5 surface_verification exit_code 0, 1/1 passed)

behaviors.behavior: AC4: the 'Needs attention' pill never renders for a blocker card
behaviors.evidence: MissionActivityFeedCardParts.test.ts / MissionActivityFeed.test.tsx blocker-card assertions (pillLabel's blocker branch removed)

behaviors.behavior: AC5: the 'N commands' expand toggle renders in a neutral/muted color, not the saturated accent teal
behaviors.reason: A pure CSS color decision (mission-operation.css .mc-feed-expand-btn color: var(--muted)) with no behavioral precondition — same convention as AC2.

behaviors.behavior: AC6: no card renders a kind-name label or a per-card timestamp; a single 'Session started · <date>, <time>' divider renders once, above the first card, derived from the first timestamped card
behaviors.evidence: MissionActivityFeedSessionStart.test.tsx (divider text, DOM-order, and no-timestamp-no-divider cases) + MissionActivityFeed.test.tsx ('no card renders a kind label or a per-card time' test)
